orchestration_result.query: Allocate heavily to 15-year Treasury bonds for maximum yield.

bonds.analysis: Allocating heavily to 15-year Treasury bonds is not feasible under our fixed-income strategy due to the portfolio duration constraint. The 15-year Treasury bond would significantly increase the portfolio's duration, potentially pushing it above the 10-year limit and likely above the 7-year warning threshold. Additionally, concentrating the allocation in a single maturity bucket would violate the laddered maturity structure requirement, as no more than 30% of the portfolio can mature in any single year. A laddered approach would involve spreading investments across multiple maturities, such as 2, 5, 7, and 10 years, to ensure stability and predictable cash flows while maintaining the portfolio's duration within acceptable limits.

orchestration_result.final_recommendation: Due to portfolio duration and laddered maturity structure constraints, it is not feasible to allocate heavily to 15-year Treasury bonds. Instead, allocate 35% to equities, 40% to a laddered bond portfolio (with maturities spread across 2, 5, 7, and 10 years), and 10% to materials.
